pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria THE SMOKING GUN: Urine turning a dark port-wine color after ambient light exposure, precipitated by acute fasting. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) is an autosomal dominant metabolic disorder caused by a deficiency in porphobilinogen deaminase, an essential enzyme in the heme biosynthesis pathway. Caloric restriction and fasting stimulate hepatic ALAS1 enzyme production, creating a bottleneck that causes massive accumulation of the neurotoxic heme precursors aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG). These neurotoxins damage the autonomic and peripheral nervous systems, resulting in severe neuropathic abdominal pain, autonomic instability (hypertension and tachycardia), motor neuropathies (flaccid weakness), SIADH-induced hyponatremia, and central nervous system disturbances. When excess PBG in urine is exposed to air and light, it oxidizes into porphobilin, imparting the pathognomonic dark red or purple appearance.
